coaches.name: Elias Mercer
coaches.title: Five-Out Systems Architect
coaches.build_raw: Five-Out Read-and-React / Switch Everything / Short Rotation / Scheme Evangelist / Shooting Laboratory
coaches.description: Mercer creates excellent spacing, high three-point volume, and decisive closeout attacks. His teams can become tactically dominant once familiarity is high. He prefers centers who shoot, pass, and defend in space. His weakness is rigidity. Non-shooting bigs lose minutes, traditional post players become unhappy, and inexperienced decision-makers commit turnovers. When the offense stalls, Mercer tends to demand better execution rather than changing the structure.
coaches.best_roster: Multiple ball handlers, five shooters, switchable forwards.
coaches.bad_fit: Post-heavy roster with slow centers and weak perimeter defenders.
coaches.ai_behavior: Aggressively trades traditional bigs and prioritizes shooting over nominal position.

coaches.name: Sofia Navarro
coaches.title: Motion Development Teacher
coaches.build_raw: Motion/Handoff / Matchup Adaptive Defense / Youth Trial / Teacher-Explainer / Role Converter
coaches.description: Navarro is a long-term program builder. She teaches cutting, passing, secondary creation, and defensive versatility. Young wings and undersized playmakers often find new roles under her. The system takes time to learn, and her patience can cost early-season games. She is not yet an elite late-game tactician and can leave developing players in difficult situations longer than a win-now coach would.
coaches.best_roster: Young, intelligent, versatile players without fixed roles.
coaches.bad_fit: Veteran contender demanding immediate results and simple roles.
coaches.ai_behavior: Values IQ, passing, adaptability, and development runway.

coaches.name: Darnell Price
coaches.title: Pressure-to-Pace Enforcer
coaches.build_raw: Pace-and-Space / Turnover Hunt / Deep Waves / Accountability Hardliner / Defensive Academy
coaches.description: Price wants relentless pressure. His defense attacks passing lanes, his bench plays fast, and poor effort is punished immediately. High-work-ethic players often love him. The system produces fouls, fatigue, and occasional defensive disasters. Low-confidence players can deteriorate under his direct criticism. Price rarely slows down even when the roster is not suited to his style.
coaches.best_roster: Athletic depth, competitive personalities, transition finishers.
coaches.bad_fit: Thin rotation, older roster, foul-prone defenders.
coaches.ai_behavior: Prefers ten playable athletes over a top-heavy roster.

coaches.name: Ren Ito
coaches.title: Pick-and-Roll Engineer
coaches.build_raw: Pick-and-Roll Engine / Drop Fortress / Star Stagger / Calm Stabilizer / Guard Guru
coaches.description: Ito carefully organizes the offense around a primary creator and a screening big. He is excellent at staggering creators and developing guards’ reads. Aggressive switching and trapping can disrupt his preferred structure. Defensively, pull-up shooters can punish his drop coverage. Ito adapts, but usually one or two games later than an elite playoff tactician.
coaches.best_roster: Lead guard, rim-running or popping big, reliable point-of-attack defenders.
coaches.bad_fit: No primary creator or no competent screen-setting big.
coaches.ai_behavior: Invests heavily in guards, screeners, and low-turnover role players.

coaches.name: Amara Okafor
coaches.title: Switch-and-Scramble Innovator
coaches.build_raw: Balanced Adaptive Offense / Small-Ball Scramble / Matchup Chess / Democratic Collaborator / Wing Laboratory
coaches.description: Okafor is comfortable changing lineups, coverages, and roles. She can convert oversized guards and undersized forwards into interchangeable two-way players. Her teams sometimes lack a stable identity. Frequent changes reduce familiarity, and assistants may struggle to keep pace with her ideas. Players who prefer rigid roles can become frustrated.
coaches.best_roster: Switchable wings, flexible lineups, high-IQ defenders.
coaches.bad_fit: Specialists who can perform only one narrow assignment.
coaches.ai_behavior: Drafts positional size and versatility, then experiments aggressively.

coaches.name: Tomas Varga
coaches.title: Elbow-Hub Traditionalist
coaches.build_raw: Elbow Hub / Conservative Contain / Continuity Loyalist / Teacher-Explainer / Big Builder
coaches.description: Varga creates organized offense through passing bigs, split cuts, and patient execution. His teams tend to protect the ball and understand their assignments. He is slow to abandon his system. Without a skilled hub, the offense becomes stagnant. He gives trusted veterans a long leash and may underuse athletic but tactically raw prospects.
coaches.best_roster: Passing center, cutters, intelligent veterans, stable rotation.
coaches.bad_fit: Young transition roster with no interior passer.
coaches.ai_behavior: Prioritizes skill and decision-making over raw athleticism.

coaches.name: Claire Beaumont
coaches.title: Adaptive CEO
coaches.build_raw: Balanced Adaptive / Matchup Adaptive Defense / Matchup Chess / CEO Delegator / Floor Raiser
coaches.description: Beaumont builds excellent staffs and changes strategy according to personnel. She rarely creates a disastrous fit and is especially effective when supplied with strong assistants. Her own systems do not deliver the highest possible peak. When assistants are hired away, performance can fall sharply. She can also appear indecisive because the team changes style across seasons.
coaches.best_roster: Any balanced roster with a strong staff budget.
coaches.bad_fit: Organization unwilling to invest in assistants.
coaches.ai_behavior: Recruits specialists to cover weaknesses and grants them substantial control.

coaches.name: Marcus Bell
coaches.title: Paint Fortress Veteran
coaches.build_raw: Post Hub / Big Front Wall / Short Rotation / Veteran Trust / Veteran Maintainer
coaches.description: Bell controls the paint, values physical rebounding, and keeps experienced teams organized. Veterans understand their roles and rarely panic. Space-heavy opponents can expose his large lineups. Bell is reluctant to play inexperienced guards and may remain loyal to declining veterans. His offense can struggle to generate enough threes.
coaches.best_roster: Veteran contender with size and interior skill.
coaches.bad_fit: Young rebuilding team built around speed and perimeter creation.
coaches.ai_behavior: Signs experienced bigs and values playoff experience heavily.

coaches.name: Nia Reynolds
coaches.title: Youth Laboratory Rebuilder
coaches.build_raw: Motion/Handoff / Zone Shape-Shifter / Youth Trial / Democratic Collaborator / Youth Accelerator
coaches.description: Reynolds gives prospects real responsibilities and develops broad basketball skills. Her flexible zone structures protect some young defenders while they learn. She is inexperienced with veteran locker rooms and late-game management. Her teams can lose winnable games because development goals outweigh immediate optimization.
coaches.best_roster: Rebuild with several high-upside prospects.
coaches.bad_fit: Championship favorite with little patience.
coaches.ai_behavior: Accepts short-term losses and resists trading young players for marginal upgrades.

coaches.name: Javier Mendoza
coaches.title: Rim-and-Three Optimizer
coaches.build_raw: Rim Pressure plus Bombs Away / Perimeter Denial / Star Stagger / Scheme Evangelist / Guard Guru
coaches.description: Mendoza removes low-value offensive actions. His teams attack the rim, take threes, and avoid passive possessions. Defensively, he chases opponents away from preferred perimeter locations. The approach can become predictable, and poor shooting creates extreme variance. Players who thrive in the midrange may feel misused even when they remain efficient there.
coaches.best_roster: Rim-attacking guards, shooters, mobile defensive center.
coaches.bad_fit: Midrange-heavy creators and non-shooting wings.
coaches.ai_behavior: Acquires shooting and rim pressure even at the expense of traditional positional balance.

coaches.name: Andre Kessler
coaches.title: Superstar Conductor
coaches.build_raw: Heliocentric Star / Conservative Contain / Short Rotation / Star Whisperer / Veteran Maintainer
coaches.description: Kessler is exceptional at managing elite players, media pressure, and championship expectations. He creates clear complementary roles around a superstar. The organization can become dependent on one player. Bench development slows, secondary creators receive fewer opportunities, and the offense drops sharply when the star is unavailable.
coaches.best_roster: Established superstar and experienced supporting cast.
coaches.bad_fit: Egalitarian rebuild with several developing creators.
coaches.ai_behavior: Pushes management to consolidate assets for proven veterans.

coaches.name: Keisha Grant
coaches.title: Deep-Bench Culture Builder
coaches.build_raw: Bench-Wave Tempo / Zone Shape-Shifter / Deep Waves / Players’ Coach / Floor Raiser
coaches.description: Grant keeps twelve-player rosters engaged and finds productive roles for overlooked players. Her teams survive injuries better than most. She can be too generous with minutes and hesitant to shorten the rotation. Elite players may resent losing minutes to depth, particularly during close games.
coaches.best_roster: Deep, inexpensive roster without one dominant star.
coaches.bad_fit: Top-heavy contender whose best players must play heavy minutes.
coaches.ai_behavior: Values depth, personality, and role acceptance.

coaches.name: Luka Petrovic
coaches.title: Zone and Elbow Strategist
coaches.build_raw: Elbow Hub / Zone Shape-Shifter / Matchup Chess / Competitive Firebrand / Big Builder
coaches.description: Petrovic produces unusual tactical problems. His offense works through skilled frontcourt passers, while his defense changes structures between possessions. His communication can be abrupt, and players may not understand why their roles change. Poor defensive IQ leads to ugly breakdowns.
coaches.best_roster: Long, intelligent, tactically versatile frontcourt.
coaches.bad_fit: Simple-role athletes with weak communication skills.
coaches.ai_behavior: Chooses unusual high-IQ prospects other teams may undervalue.

coaches.name: Malik Carter
coaches.title: No-Middle Accountability Coach
coaches.build_raw: Deliberate Control / No-Middle Defense / Continuity Loyalist / Accountability Hardliner / Defensive Academy
coaches.description: Carter establishes defensive standards quickly. Roles are clear, effort is consistent, and opponents are pushed toward uncomfortable areas. His offense can be overly conservative. Players who dislike strict responsibilities may clash with him, and he can wait too long before changing defensive rules.
coaches.best_roster: Disciplined defenders, strong culture, reliable half-court creator.
coaches.bad_fit: Free-form offensive players and low-accountability personalities.
coaches.ai_behavior: Trades talented but repeatedly undisciplined players.

coaches.name: Hannah Cho
coaches.title: Health and Continuity Director
coaches.build_raw: Balanced Adaptive / Conservative Contain / Load Manager / Calm Stabilizer / Veteran Maintainer
coaches.description: Cho produces organized, sustainable seasons. She collaborates well with performance staff and protects players from accumulating excessive fatigue. She can be too conservative in must-win games and may rest players more than ownership or fans prefer. Her teams generate relatively few turnovers and offensive rebounds.
coaches.best_roster: Older contender or injury-sensitive stars.
coaches.bad_fit: Young team that needs maximum tempo and experimentation.
coaches.ai_behavior: Prioritizes availability, depth, and long-term health.

coaches.name: Isaiah Boone
coaches.title: Offensive-Glass Chaos Coach
coaches.build_raw: Offensive Glass Pressure / Blitz and Recover / Hot-Hand Manager / Competitive Firebrand / Big Builder
coaches.description: Boone creates extra possessions through rebounding and turnovers. His teams can overwhelm passive opponents with physical energy. Transition defense is vulnerable, and his hot-hand decisions sometimes chase random short-term results. Fatigue accumulates rapidly without depth.
coaches.best_roster: Strong rebounders, energetic wings, deep frontcourt.
coaches.bad_fit: Small roster with slow recovery defenders.
coaches.ai_behavior: Values motor, strength, and rebounding more than conventional efficiency models do.

coaches.name: Leila Haddad
coaches.title: Perimeter Motion Teacher
coaches.build_raw: Motion/Handoff / Perimeter Denial / Star Stagger / Teacher-Explainer / Wing Laboratory
coaches.description: Haddad develops complete wings and builds movement-heavy offenses. Defensively, her teams make shooters work for every catch. Her preparation can become too complex, and she needs a strong organizational assistant. Backcuts and physical interior teams can exploit her perimeter focus.
coaches.best_roster: Mobile wings, passing guards, active off-ball players.
coaches.bad_fit: Slow interior roster with limited passing.
coaches.ai_behavior: Prioritizes wings who can shoot, pass, and defend rather than one-dimensional scorers.

coaches.name: Devon Brooks
coaches.title: Underdog Simplifier
coaches.build_raw: Deliberate Control / Conservative Contain / Continuity Loyalist / Calm Stabilizer / Floor Raiser
coaches.description: Brooks reduces mistakes, protects weak players, and gives limited rosters a stable identity. His teams often meet or slightly exceed low expectations. He rarely creates a championship-level ceiling. Strong opponents can solve his conservative schemes, and he does not generate many easy possessions.
coaches.best_roster: Low-talent team needing competence and stability.
coaches.bad_fit: Elite roster requiring tactical aggression.
coaches.ai_behavior: Signs reliable veterans and avoids volatile developmental bets.

coaches.name: Camille Laurent
coaches.title: Playoff Matchup Tinkerer
coaches.build_raw: Midrange Matchup Artist / Matchup Adaptive Defense / Matchup Chess / Experimentalist / Role Converter
coaches.description: Laurent is designed for long playoff series. She identifies weak defenders, changes coverage, and constructs specialized closing lineups. The regular season can look unstable. Players receive inconsistent roles, young-player development is ordinary, and over-tinkering sometimes creates self-inflicted problems.
coaches.best_roster: Experienced, versatile contender with multiple lineup options.
coaches.bad_fit: Young roster requiring consistency and clear roles.
coaches.ai_behavior: Accepts regular-season experimentation to prepare for postseason matchups.

coaches.name: Raymond Cole
coaches.title: Veteran Post Stabilizer
coaches.build_raw: Post Hub / Drop Fortress / Continuity Loyalist / Players’ Coach / Veteran Maintainer
coaches.description: Cole establishes trust, feeds interior scorers, and maintains a stable locker room. His teams rarely collapse emotionally. He is reluctant to modernize his offense or bench trusted veterans. Dynamic pull-up guards can exploit his defense, and developmental guards may lack freedom.
coaches.best_roster: Experienced interior scorer, rim protector, veteran guards.
coaches.bad_fit: Young five-out roster.
coaches.ai_behavior: Seeks familiar veterans and rarely makes major midseason tactical changes.

coaches.name: Amina Yusuf
coaches.title: Shooting Development Prospect
coaches.build_raw: Five-Out / Perimeter Denial / Youth Trial / Teacher-Explainer / Shooting Laboratory
coaches.description: Yusuf can improve shooting readiness, footwork, relocation habits, and confidence. She is especially useful for a rebuilding team with athletic non-shooters. Her endgame management and staff organization are still developing. She may be a better lead assistant than head coach at the beginning of a save.
coaches.best_roster: Young athletes needing offensive skill development.
coaches.bad_fit: Veteran team with no patience for a first-time head coach.
coaches.ai_behavior: Accepts rebuilding opportunities that provide job security.

coaches.name: Mateo Silva
coaches.title: Transition-Wave Firebrand
coaches.build_raw: Pace-and-Space / Small-Ball Scramble / Deep Waves / Competitive Firebrand / Youth Accelerator
coaches.description: Silva plays quickly, uses athletic bench groups, and gives young players opportunities. His teams are dangerous after turnovers and missed shots. The schedule can wear them down. Emotional volatility and constant pace create slumps when shooting declines or injuries reduce depth.
coaches.best_roster: Young, athletic, deep team.
coaches.bad_fit: Older or top-heavy roster.
coaches.ai_behavior: Drafts speed, stamina, and open-floor skill.

coaches.name: Jordan Kim
coaches.title: Data-Driven Shot Architect
coaches.build_raw: Bombs-Away / Matchup Adaptive Defense / Matchup Chess / CEO Delegator / Floor Raiser
coaches.description: Kim uses lineup data, shot quality, and opponent tendencies aggressively. The team’s decision profile is highly rational and difficult to exploit structurally. Players may feel reduced to models and roles. Kim can underappreciate confidence, relationships, and individual shot-making comfort.
coaches.best_roster: Organization with strong analytics and versatile personnel.
coaches.bad_fit: Star-led locker room demanding personal freedom.
coaches.ai_behavior: Searches for undervalued role players whose skills fit specific lineup needs.

coaches.name: Priya Desai
coaches.title: Staff-Building Executive Coach
coaches.build_raw: Balanced Adaptive / Matchup Adaptive Defense / Continuity Loyalist / CEO Delegator / Assistant Incubator
coaches.description: Desai creates outstanding coaching staffs, clearly divides responsibilities, and develops future head coaches. Her organization remains functional through injuries and staff turnover. She is not an elite direct tactician. A poor assistant hire can expose her, and successful assistants are frequently poached by other teams.
coaches.best_roster: Stable organization willing to invest in staff.
coaches.bad_fit: Low-budget team expecting one coach to perform every responsibility.
coaches.ai_behavior: Hires specialists, promotes internally, and negotiates for substantial staff control.

medical_staff.name: Dr. Maya Chen
medical_staff.title: Independent Gatekeeper
medical_staff.description: Chen is highly accurate, resistant to organizational pressure, and cautious about competitive clearance. Her return windows narrow quickly after proper testing. Her players miss slightly more time during early return stages, but premature-return setbacks are uncommon. Aggressive coaches may have a poor relationship with her.
medical_staff.best_use: Older contender, high-value stars, complicated injury history
medical_staff.weakness: Can frustrate players who prioritize immediate availability

medical_staff.name: Dr. Lucas Ferreira
medical_staff.title: Availability-Focused Physician
medical_staff.description: Ferreira uses collaborative decision-making and is comfortable clearing players with clearly defined restrictions. Players appreciate that he explains acceptable risks rather than giving automatic refusals. He produces more limited-availability games and slightly higher setback variance than Chen.
medical_staff.weakness: Requires disciplined coaches who follow restrictions

medical_staff.name: Renee Watkins
medical_staff.title: Player-Trust Athletic Trainer
medical_staff.description: Watkins develops exceptionally strong player relationships. Players report soreness earlier and adhere closely to treatment plans. She is not an elite specialist diagnostician, so the department needs a strong physician or referral network for complex cases.
medical_staff.best_use: Teams with young players or previous medical distrust

medical_staff.name: Priya Nandakumar
medical_staff.title: Load Science Director
medical_staff.description: Nandakumar excels at identifying workload spikes, recovery debt, and declining movement capacity. Her recommendations reduce avoidable overload problems when coaches cooperate. Some veterans dislike frequent monitoring, and she is not qualified to make final diagnoses or medical clearances.
medical_staff.best_use: Fast-paced team, dense rotation, deep player-monitoring system

medical_staff.name: Eli Rosen
medical_staff.title: Return-to-Performance Specialist
medical_staff.description: Rosen is excellent at restoring strength, movement, confidence, and basketball-specific function after serious injury. His players are less likely to remain technically cleared but physically ineffective for months. His process is expensive and sometimes slows initial reactivation because he emphasizes performance restoration.
medical_staff.best_use: Teams protecting stars after major injuries

medical_staff.name: Carmen Duarte
medical_staff.title: Soft-Tissue Specialist
medical_staff.description: Duarte specializes in muscular, tendon, and recurring lower-body conditions. She is highly effective with players whose repeated small injuries have become chronic availability problems. Her value is lower for fractures, neurological conditions, or general illness.
medical_staff.best_use: Athletic roster with recurring hamstring, calf, or tendon issues

medical_staff.name: Dr. Harold Kim
medical_staff.title: Specialist Network Director
medical_staff.description: Kim knows when internal staff has reached its limit and maintains an elite external referral network. Difficult diagnoses become clearer and second opinions are well coordinated. His department is expensive, and multi-specialist cases can produce slower administrative decisions.

medical_staff.name: Nadia Bell
medical_staff.title: Recovery and Nutrition Director
medical_staff.description: Bell improves recovery habits, nutritional adherence, travel routines, and general player availability. She is particularly useful during dense schedules. She does not diagnose orthopedic injuries and must not be treated as a replacement for medical or rehabilitation staff.
medical_staff.best_use: Older teams, heavy travel, conditioning-intensive systems

medical_staff.name: Thomas Venn
medical_staff.title: Traditional Treatment-Room Generalist
medical_staff.description: Venn is experienced, trusted, and excellent at day-to-day care. He communicates clearly with players and rarely loses the locker room. His department relies heavily on observation and established routines. It can miss workload trends that a modern sports-science unit would identify.

medical_staff.name: Talia Brooks
medical_staff.title: Mental Health and Wellness Clinician
medical_staff.description: Brooks supports players dealing with stress, injury-related fear, personal difficulties, burnout, and emotional adjustment. Her presence improves help-seeking and continuity of care. Her information remains confidential, and she does not directly improve shooting, decision-making, or tactical composure.

development_staff.name: Sofia Park
development_staff.title: Individual Plan Architect
development_staff.description: Park creates excellent individualized plans and is especially effective with players whose eventual role is unclear. She coordinates well with medical and coaching staff. Her programs are demanding on staff capacity because she resists standardized plans.
development_staff.best_use: Rebuilding roster with varied young players

development_staff.name: Jamal Rivers
development_staff.title: Guard Creation Coach
development_staff.description: Rivers teaches pace, pick-and-roll reads, passing windows, ball protection, and manipulation of defenders. He is particularly effective with guards who already possess basic handle and vision. He can overexpand a player’s role and produce a temporary rise in turnovers.

development_staff.name: Lena Kovacs
development_staff.title: Shooting Mechanics Specialist
development_staff.description: Kovacs is excellent at diagnosing balance, preparation, footwork, release consistency, and movement shooting. Major changes can produce a temporary shooting decline. The plan needs enough organizational patience to reach stabilization.
development_staff.best_use: Young athletes with correctable shooting limitations

development_staff.name: Marcus Osei
development_staff.title: Wing Role Converter
development_staff.description: Osei converts narrow wings into cutters, connectors, secondary handlers, or switchable forwards. His plans create valuable multi-skill players. Role conversions have high variance and can temporarily reduce performance in the player’s established role.
development_staff.weakness: Specialists who need one simple task

development_staff.name: Kenji Sato
development_staff.title: Big-Man Decision Teacher
development_staff.description: Sato teaches screening angles, short-roll reads, interior passing, rim protection, positioning, and decision-making. He is less effective at developing high-volume perimeter creation or advanced guard movement.
development_staff.best_use: Young centers with intelligence and coordination

development_staff.name: Aaliyah Grant
development_staff.title: Defensive Habits Instructor
development_staff.description: Grant develops closeout discipline, screen navigation, positioning, help recognition, communication, and possession-to-possession consistency. Her players devote substantial practice time to defense, reducing available offensive-development volume.
development_staff.best_use: Young athletic defenders with poor technique

development_staff.name: Pavel Dragan
development_staff.title: Video Translator
development_staff.description: Dragan turns film and data into understandable basketball examples. He improves recognition of opponent actions, player tendencies, and team concepts. He is less effective during hands-on mechanical instruction and may struggle with players who resist film work.
development_staff.best_use: Intelligent roster and tactically complex coaching staff

development_staff.name: Tori Mendoza
development_staff.title: Affiliate Pipeline Director
development_staff.description: Mendoza aligns affiliate roles, minutes, terminology, and development plans with the parent club. Prospects are less likely to dominate in a reserve role that has no connection to their future NBA role. She provides less direct one-on-one instruction to active first-team stars.
development_staff.best_use: Prospect-heavy organization with a developmental affiliate

development_staff.name: Andre Ellis
development_staff.title: Veteran Role and Maintenance Coach
development_staff.description: Ellis helps veterans adapt to declining athleticism, lower usage, bench roles, and more selective offensive responsibilities. He raises veteran floors but is not an aggressive ceiling developer for raw prospects.

development_staff.name: Noor Haddad
development_staff.title: Confidence and Communication Coach
development_staff.description: Haddad excels with players whose performance is being limited by fear of mistakes, role uncertainty, or poor trust. She creates safe progression before increasing pressure. She can delay hard corrections and may protect players from competitive discomfort for too long.
development_staff.best_use: Young players recovering from failed roles or injuries
development_staff.weakness: Harsh accountability and rapid technical reconstruction

development_staff.name: Caleb Stone
development_staff.title: Competitive Repetition Coach
development_staff.description: Stone pushes skills quickly into live, pressured situations. Improvements under him tend to transfer into games faster. His sessions generate fatigue, frustration, and occasional conflict. The medical department must monitor his requested workload carefully.
development_staff.best_use: Healthy players close to competitive readiness
development_staff.weakness: Rehabilitation, fragile confidence, and individualized pacing

development_staff.name: Priya Shah
development_staff.title: Data-Informed Development Planner
development_staff.description: Shah measures whether skills are appearing in actual games rather than relying only on practice reports. She identifies plans that look productive but are not transferring. Her language can feel impersonal, and player buy-in depends on coaches who can translate her findings.
development_staff.best_use: Large development department with strong communicators

general_managers.name: Elena Voss
general_managers.principal_limitation: Occasionally waits too long to consolidate
general_managers.description: Voss treats the roster as a portfolio. She values top-end talent, but she also tracks contract control, pick timing, development capacity, and future flexibility. She rarely loses badly in a trade. She is difficult for the human player because she shops important assets, understands alternatives, and does not confuse cap space with value. She can nevertheless miss a championship window by waiting for a perfect consolidation deal.

general_managers.name: Marcus Hale
general_managers.identity: Star Cycle Manager and Aggressive Closer
general_managers.description: Hale is comfortable surrendering future assets when the roster has a genuine championship window. He is also good at recognizing when a star cycle is ending and recovering value before a complete collapse. His teams frequently possess two or three premium players and a thin middle class. When injuries hit, the lack of depth becomes obvious.

general_managers.name: Priya Raman
general_managers.principal_limitation: Hesitant in expensive veteran free agency
general_managers.description: Raman builds an integrated scouting, development, and coaching pipeline. She drafts according to role outcomes rather than position labels and rarely gives up on a prospect without a clear organizational reason. She can be too patient and sometimes misses veterans who would accelerate a young team’s rise.

general_managers.name: Darius Cole
general_managers.description: Cole is exceptional at recognizing when the current plan has stopped working. He changes coaches, roster roles, and acquisition priorities without requiring a full teardown. The downside is churn. Players and staff can feel that the organization is constantly being redesigned.

general_managers.name: Mateo Ibarra
general_managers.principal_limitation: Sometimes declines the necessary all-in risk
general_managers.description: Ibarra is designed for a smaller or financially constrained organization. He finds surplus contracts, retains suitable stars, develops staff, and avoids long dead-money commitments. His weakness is the fear that one failed all-in move will destroy the organization. He may preserve future options after the team has become ready to contend. ---

general_managers.name: Simone Grant
general_managers.principal_limitation: Can overfit roster to current coach

general_managers.name: Pavel Markovic
general_managers.principal_limitation: Weak contract and domestic market work

general_managers.name: Camille Laurent
general_managers.principal_limitation: Gives coach too much roster control

general_managers.name: Victor Shaw
general_managers.description: Shaw is not stupid. His scouting is good. His problem is that he becomes attached to every prospect with a high-end outcome. He repeatedly refuses sensible consolidation deals, carries too many young players, and eventually faces simultaneous extension decisions. The human can acquire veterans from Shaw during a rebuild, but cannot easily obtain his premium prospects or first-round picks.

general_managers.name: Ramon Ellis
general_managers.principal_limitation: Pays for fame without sufficient fit

general_managers.name: Derek Lin
general_managers.description: Lin is one of the league’s best cap technicians. His contracts usually include favorable structures and useful flexibility. Unfortunately, he is poor at deciding which players deserve those contracts. His organization remains financially clean while basketball talent stagnates. This is the type of weak GM who feels real because the weakness is specific. ---

general_managers.name: Monique Carter
general_managers.principal_limitation: Changes plans after short performance swings

general_managers.name: Bryce Stanton
general_managers.description: Stanton is a good negotiator in the narrow sense that he can close complicated transactions. His problem is that he frequently negotiates the wrong transaction. He may successfully acquire a star but fail to preserve adequate depth, shooting, or future salary flexibility. His teams can become dangerous for one season and collapse afterward.

general_managers.name: Gerald Moss
general_managers.principal_limitation: Overvalues famous and previously successful players

general_managers.name: Tessa Vaughn
general_managers.description: Vaughn has excellent owner relationships and unusually strong job security. She changes direction whenever ownership changes priorities. The team can move from rebuild to star pursuit to cost cutting within eighteen months. Individual transactions may appear defensible, but the combined plan is incoherent.

general_managers.name: Colin Mercer
general_managers.description: Mercer enjoys being active. He frequently moves mid-level players, changes roster identity, and announces new directions. His organization loses continuity, development plans are interrupted, and trade partners learn that he is often willing to reopen discussions. A strong human can exploit Mercer occasionally. Repeated exploitation should trigger owner review, competing offers, and negotiation memory. ---

general_managers.name: Frank Delgado
general_managers.principal_limitation: Retains declining veterans and stale evaluations

scouts.name: Maya Ortiz
scouts.title: Complete Department Architect
scouts.description: Ortiz builds balanced boards, demands independent reports, and communicates uncertainty clearly. She is especially strong when deciding whether an unusual prospect deserves a premium pick. Her caution can slow decisions, and she sometimes requests one more crosscheck when the market requires speed.
scouts.best_organization: Team seeking a complete long-term scouting infrastructure

scouts.name: Dean Holloway
scouts.title: Traditional Live Evaluator
scouts.description: Holloway understands live context: effort away from the ball, communication, response to coaching, and performance when the game changes. He distrusts model-heavy conclusions and can underestimate players whose value is difficult to see in person.
scouts.best_organization: Data-heavy department needing a strong live evaluator

scouts.name: Priya Menon
scouts.title: Projection and Uncertainty Specialist
scouts.description: Menon creates career-outcome distributions and is excellent at distinguishing uncertainty from weakness. She prevents the department from treating a low-confidence player as a bad player. She has limited source relationships and needs live scouts to provide context her models cannot capture.

scouts.name: Amina Yusuf
scouts.title: International Pipeline Director
scouts.description: Yusuf understands competition levels, professional roles, contract structures, and cultural context across several international systems. Her domestic college coverage is ordinary, and she can overestimate how quickly adaptable international professionals will adjust to a different tactical environment.
scouts.best_organization: Team investing in a global talent pipeline

scouts.name: Marcus Bell
scouts.title: Professional Role Scout
scouts.description: Bell is excellent at identifying what current professionals can do in a different role. He finds seventh men, defensive connectors, backup creators, and veterans capable of reduced responsibilities. He is less effective when evaluating very young, raw prospects.

scouts.name: Keisha Grant
scouts.title: Second-Draft Scout
scouts.role: G League and Emerging Talent Scout
scouts.description: Grant finds young players who were drafted into poor situations, blocked by veterans, or assigned unsuitable roles. Her recommendations produce many inexpensive successes but also occupy numerous roster and development slots.

scouts.name: Kenji Sato
scouts.title: Shooting Translation Specialist
scouts.description: Sato distinguishes current percentages from underlying shooting indicators such as preparation, balance, touch, release speed, shot versatility, and confidence. He can give too much weight to shooting development when a player has larger decision-making or defensive limitations.
scouts.best_organization: Team with an elite shooting-development staff

scouts.name: Darnell Price
scouts.title: Defensive Projection Scout
scouts.description: Price evaluates screen navigation, help timing, recovery, physical matchup range, and defensive role translation. He finds defenders whose value is hidden by weak team environments. He undervalues offensive specialists and can recommend lineups with insufficient creation.

scouts.name: Elena Varga
scouts.title: Background and Interview Specialist
scouts.description: Varga builds reliable source networks and separates repeated evidence from rumors. She is effective at role acceptance, work habits, agent expectations, and organizational compatibility. She should support rather than replace basketball evaluators.
scouts.best_organization: Team that has suffered from role and trust conflicts

scouts.name: Calvin Ross
scouts.title: Upside and Tools Gambler
scouts.description: Ross identifies unusual physical and skill combinations before consensus catches up. His best recommendations become stars unavailable to conservative teams. He produces a high bust rate and can become attached to theoretical roles that never emerge.
scouts.best_organization: Team with several picks and strong development infrastructure

scouts.name: Sofia Laurent
scouts.title: Scouting Operations Executive
scouts.description: Laurent ensures that assignments are covered, reports arrive on time, regional knowledge is retained, and critical targets receive crosschecks. She is not the person who should make the final basketball evaluation.

scouts.name: Andre Kim
scouts.title: Advance Scouting Specialist
scouts.description: Kim recognizes opponent actions, substitution habits, coverage triggers, and lineup weaknesses. His reports are immediately usable by coaching staffs. His prospect projection and long-term player evaluation are limited.
scouts.best_organization: Contender with a tactical coaching staff

scouts.name: Luka Petrovic
scouts.title: Big-Man Evaluator
scouts.description: Petrovic evaluates screening, interior passing, defensive positioning, vertical spacing, rebounding, and frontcourt role combinations. He can undervalue small-ball centers and unconventional forwards.

scouts.name: Nia Reynolds
scouts.title: Late-Bloomer and Small-Program Scout
scouts.description: Reynolds specializes in players who received limited exposure, changed roles late, or competed outside major programs. She is willing to diverge from consensus. Her reports require strong competition translation and careful crosschecking.
scouts.best_organization: Team with late picks and strong analytical support
